description: Verify that DUT replies to an ARP Request carrying proto_type=IPv4 (0x0800) — receiver must accept the standard upper-layer family (RFC 826 §2.4)
approach:
[Objective]
Positive control for ARP_27 (rejection of unknown proto_type). With proto_type set to the standard IPv4 identifier, DUT must reply normally.

[Scenario — chronological]
1. Tester → DUT: ARP Request injected
   • opcode       = 1
   • proto_type   = 0x0800 (IPv4)   ← correct
   • target_ip    = DUT IP
   • sender_*     = HOST-1-IP / MAC-ADDR1

2. Observation (3 s window):
   • DUT → Tester: ARP Reply (opcode 2, sender_mac=DUT, target_ip=HOST-1-IP)

[Pass condition]
DUT emits an ARP Reply within the observation window.

[Fail condition]
Fail_no_reply — DUT did not reply despite proto_type being the standard IPv4 identifier.

verdicts.Pass: DUT replied to a Request with proto_type=IPv4 — normal
verdicts.Fail_no_reply: DUT did not reply even with proto_type=0x0800 — reception logic broken for valid input
